name: Drought
value: Sudan harvest failure; no famine declared
summary: Crop Monitor rates Sudan's main-season crops a failure after record-dry rains; no drought famine declaration found
state: GEOGLAM's Crop Monitor of 5 Nov rates Sudan's main-season crops a failure after delayed, below-average rains and conflict, ranks June–September among the driest on record across much of South Sudan, and reports drought in northern Ethiopia, Chad, Niger, Mali and South Africa's Western Cape wheat region (Crop Monitor). An IPC alert in October warned of growing famine risk in Darfur and Kordofan from war and El Niño-linked drought (IRC, 13 Oct). Sudan is not a major exporter, so severe drought in crop regions keeps Watch; searches on 19 Nov found no new famine declaration.
for_you: Drought in East Africa and the Sahel mainly affects local food supply and humanitarian needs rather than global grain prices. El Niño raises the chance of a dry November–March season in southern Africa.
rubric_hit: Watch: severe drought in major crop regions (Sudan crop failure, Ethiopia, Sahel); no famine declaration or major exporter harvest failure for Alert

sources.title: GEOGLAM Crop Monitor — Crop Monitor for Early Warning, November 2026
IRC — War and El Niño-driven drought deplete food stocks, pushing Sudan further towards famine

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
